claims.text: An ML approach incorporating force-constant fluctuations and local chemical disorder will identify low-phonon-thermal-conductivity HEAs more accurately than methods based only on mass and size descriptors.
Conventional predictive methods for these HEAs are based solely or primarily on elemental mass and atomic-size parameters.
FeCoCrMnNi-like HEAs can provide a single-phase, chemically homogeneous initial material state after conventional melting and homogenization.
Local chemical disorder and force-constant fluctuations enhance phonon scattering in HEAs.
Enhanced local disorder in multi-principal-element alloys produces larger interatomic force-constant fluctuations.
Force-constant fluctuations scatter or attenuate heat-carrying phonons.
Stronger phonon scattering reduces phonon lifetimes.
Force-constant and local chemical fluctuations lower lattice thermal conductivity through enhanced phonon scattering.
Descriptors capturing force-constant and local-bond fluctuations can be used by an ML model to identify compositions with enhanced phonon scattering.
HEAs selected by the proposed model will have lattice thermal conductivities approximately 20–30% lower than values predicted by conventional descriptor-based models.
A measured conductivity 20–30% below a conventional model's prediction demonstrates improved prediction accuracy.
Mass- and size-based predictive methods have had limited success differentiating HEAs with very low thermal conductivity.
The proposed predictive improvement applies primarily to single-phase, chemically homogeneous HEAs.
Significant phase separation or chemical inhomogeneity would limit the proposed model's applicability.
The approach may fail when precipitates, oxidation, or other scattering mechanisms dominate thermal transport.
The quantitative improvement in prediction accuracy depends on the availability and quality of training data describing force-constant fluctuations.
Variations in synthesis and measurement conditions can affect the observed thermal-transport outcome.

contradictions.description: The central claim concerns improved prediction accuracy, which requires comparing prediction errors on held-out materials. The predicted outcome and falsification rule instead compare measured conductivity with the conventional model's predicted conductivity. A material being at least 20% below a conventional prediction does not by itself show that the new model predicted it more accurately. The uncertainty field separately refers to reduction in prediction error, so the operational endpoints are inconsistent.
